title: LECTURE 5 (Random variables; Probability mass function (PMF); Expectation; Variance)
topics: Random variables as functions from the sample space Omega to the reals (discrete or continuous values)
Notation: random variable X vs numerical value x; several r.v.'s on the same sample space
Probability mass function p_X(x) = P(X=x) = P({omega in Omega s.t. X(omega)=x}); nonnegativity and normalization
Recipe for computing a PMF (collect outcomes, add probabilities, repeat for all x)
Geometric PMF: number of coin tosses until first head, p_X(k) = (1-p)^{k-1} p
Binomial PMF: number of heads in n independent tosses, p_X(k) = C(n,k) p^k (1-p)^{n-k}
Discrete uniform PMF on 0,1,...,n
Expectation E[X] = sum_x x p_X(x); center-of-gravity and long-run-average interpretations
Expected value rule for functions of a r.v.: E[g(X)] = sum_x g(x) p_X(x) (easy way vs hard way via p_Y)
Caution: E[g(X)] != g(E[X]) in general
Linearity properties E[alpha], E[alpha X], E[alpha X + beta]
Second moment E[X^2]
Variance var(X) = E[(X-E[X])^2] = E[X^2] - (E[X])^2; var(X) >= 0; var(alpha X + beta) = alpha^2 var(X)
